title: Restriction of scalars through a pseudo-coherent algebra
statement: Let $f:S\to T$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. Suppose that $T[0]$, regarded as a complex of $S$-modules through $f$, is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. For every $K\in D(T)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], one has $$K\text{ is pseudo-coherent over }T\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f_*K\text{ is pseudo-coherent over }S.$$ Here $f_*$ is restriction of scalars: it applies the ordinary forgetful functor termwise to complexes, keeping the same additive groups and differentials, and uses the action $s\cdot k=f(s)k$. No flatness, surjectivity, or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 064Z, lemma-finite-push-pseudo-coherent, final assertion (pseudo-coherence, rather than the m-pseudo-coherent refinement).

proof.text: Restriction leaves kernels, images and quotient additive groups unchanged: $H^i(f_*C)=f_*H^i(C)$. It preserves quasi-isomorphisms and the explicit cone $\operatorname{Cone}(u)^i=C^{i+1}\oplus D^i$ with its signed differential. Thus it acts on the derived categories and preserves cone triangles. Choose a bounded-above finite free $S$-resolution $P$ representing $T[0]$. For each finite $r$, the complex $P^{\oplus r}$ is still bounded above and finite free and represents $(f_*T^{\oplus r})[0]$. Hence every finite free $T$-module is pseudo-coherent over $S$, including the rank-zero module.

source.place: Tag 064Z, restriction of scalars and the finite free terms; Tag 064Q, definition-pseudo-coherent

proof.text: If $K$ is pseudo-coherent over $T$, choose a bounded-above finite free $T$-complex $E$ representing it. Every term of $f_*E$ is pseudo-coherent over $S$ by step 1. Apply [lem-sfb-pseudocoherent-terms-bounded-above] over $S$. Since restriction preserves quasi-isomorphisms, its conclusion is precisely pseudo-coherence of $f_*K$.

Conversely suppose $f_*K$ is pseudo-coherent. Represent $K$ by a $T$-complex $C$. A bounded-above finite free model for $f_*C$ supplies an integer $b$ with $H^i(C)=0$ for $i>b$, since the cohomology groups are unchanged. Fix any bounded finite free $T$-complex $F$, chain map $u:F\to C$, and integer $n$ with $H^i(\operatorname{Cone}(u))=0$ for $i>n$. By step 1 its restricted terms are pseudo-coherent; [lem-sfb-pseudocoherent-terms-bounded-above] makes $f_*F$ pseudo-coherent.

source.place: Tag 064Z, reverse direction; Tag 064U, finite-cone construction

proof.text: For every integer $m$, apply [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-iff-all-m] to obtain $(m+1)$-pseudo-coherence of $f_*F$ and $m$-pseudo-coherence of $f_*C$. The first clause of [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-distinguished-triangle] applied to their cone triangle gives $m$-pseudo-coherence of $f_*\operatorname{Cone}(u)$. Apply the equivalence again, for all $m$, to obtain pseudo-coherence of that restricted cone.

In particular the restricted cone is $n$-pseudo-coherent by [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-iff-all-m]. Its cohomology vanishes above $n$, so [lem-sc-finite-cohomology] over $S$ shows that $H^n(\operatorname{Cone}(u))$ is finitely generated as an $S$-module. The same finite generators generate over $T$: an expression $x=\sum s_jx_j$ becomes $x=\sum f(s_j)x_j$. Thus its top cohomology is a finite $T$-module.

source.place: Tag 064S, lemma-finite-cohomology; Tag 064U, descending finite-free construction

proof.text: The arbitrary choices in step 3 and the conclusion of step 5 verify every cone-finiteness hypothesis of [lem-pc-ring-finite-cone-free-model] for $R=T$, the complex $C$, and the bound $b$. Choose one universe containing $S,T,C$ and all the complexes quantified there. The criterion supplies a chain-level quasi-isomorphism $Q\to C$ with $Q^i=0$ for $i>b$ and every $Q^i$ finite free over $T$. This is exactly pseudo-coherence of $K$ over $T$. Together with step 2 it proves the asserted equivalence.
